record.original_question: For contextual deduction, a rewriting-like clausal reasoning mechanism that uses pattern matching rather than unification and instantiates clauses only to match existing clauses, is there a useful notion of complete theory under which contextual deduction is complete for refuting ground clauses?

evidence.quote: Is there a notion of “complete theory” for which contextual deduction is complete for refutation of ground clauses?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following clausal reasoning mechanism, called contextual deduction. Clauses are finite disjunctions of literals in first-order logic. Contextual deduction is a rewriting-like inference system on clauses that, unlike resolution, uses pattern matching instead of full unification: a clause C may be used to simplify or reduce another clause D only by instantiating C (via a substitution applied to its variables) so that the instantiated literals of C syntactically match literals already present in D, with no instantiation of D permitted. In particular, no new terms are introduced into the clause set by the inference rule.

The system is to be used as a refutation procedure for ground clauses: given a set S of (possibly non-ground) clauses together with a finite set G of ground clauses, the goal is to derive the empty clause from S ∪ G using contextual deduction whenever S ∪ G is unsatisfiable.

Because contextual deduction never instantiates clauses except to match literals already in the current clause set, it is in general incomplete for first-order refutation. The problem is the following:

Does there exist a useful and non-trivial notion of "complete theory" T (i.e., a class of clause sets, defined by some natural closure or saturation condition) such that, whenever S belongs to this class T and G is any finite set of ground clauses with S ∪ G unsatisfiable, contextual deduction is guaranteed to derive the empty clause from S ∪ G? Identify and characterize such a notion of complete theory, or prove that no useful such notion exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for "contextual deduction" and refutational completeness for ground clauses did not return results addressing this specific question. No published resolution of the problem could be verified, but neither could a clear statement that it remains open. The status is therefore unknown from the available search evidence.

status_evidence.title: Resolution Theorem Proving (Bachmair, Ganzinger)
status_evidence.snippet: General treatment of refutational completeness for clausal inference systems based on ordering and saturation, but does not address contextual deduction as defined here.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references on refutational completeness do not appear to settle the contextual-deduction question.

status_evidence.title: A General Refutational Completeness Result for an Inference Procedure Based on Associative-Commutative Unification
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes refutational completeness for inference procedures using unification, not pattern matching as in contextual deduction.
status_evidence.claim: Existing completeness results target unification-based systems rather than the matching-only contextual-deduction mechanism.
